scope: Original critical synthesis for Strategy 1. Papers are not independent replications of the local 30-minute ES/MES rule. No licensed market dataset or historical replication was obtained.
access_note: SSRN landing pages and public author-hosted PDFs were read with the web retrieval tool. Direct sandbox PDF downloads failed with SSL EOF. No source PDFs are redistributed. Long PDFs are limited to the first 30 PDF pages by retrieval; selective reads are explicitly identified below.

sources.title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market
sources.authors: Carlo Zarattini, Andrea Barbon, Andrew Aziz
sources.access: SSRN abstract and all 7 retrieved PDF chunks, including methods, Tables 1-5 and references; complete retrievable paper text.
sources.version: First version 16 February 2024 on PDF; SSRN lists revision 29 April 2025. Author-hosted copy accessed 8 September 2026; upload directory date is not research sample date.

facts.sample: US stocks 2016-01-01 through 2023-12-31; about 7,000 stocks; CRSP universe, IQFeed intraday; delisted stocks included per authors
facts.rules: 5-minute range direction; stop entry at high/low; 10% of prior 14-day ATR stop; EOD exit; opening price >$5, prior 14-day average volume >=1m shares, ATR >$0.50; relative opening volume >=1 and top 20 for selected version; $0.0035/share commission; 4x leverage cap
facts.relative_volume_mean_net_r: Below 1x: -0.02R; above 1x: +0.08R; above 30x: +0.38R. Nested thresholds, not independent portfolios.

sources.limits: Not an ES test, not an EMA20/50 test; 14-day ATR differs from 14 five-minute bars. Capital allocation and path execution need replication. Hit Ratio kept under author's label, not assumed to be per-trade win rate. Exact drawdown episode dates unavailable. Commission inclusion is not a full execution-cost audit.

sources.title: Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable?
sources.access: SSRN abstract and all 5 retrieved PDF chunks; complete retrievable paper text.
sources.locators: Section 2 and Table 1; Section 3 and Table 2; Section 4 and Figures 7-8.

facts.sample: 2016-01-01 through 2023-02-17; Interactive Brokers aggregated data; QQQ/TQQQ
facts.rules: Entry at second five-minute candle open in direction of first candle; doji skipped; opposite first-candle extreme stop; 10R target or EOD; 1% risk budget, $25k initial, 4x leverage, commission $0.0005/share, no slippage
facts.qqq_prose: 1,795 trades; 24% trade win rate; +0.13R average; 675% total return, 31% annualized return, Sharpe 1.12 in prose; these differ from Table 2.
facts.tqqq_prose: +0.18R average; 46% annualized return in prose vs 48% Yearly Return in Table 2.
facts.optimization: Section 4 reports 9,350% return and $25,000 growing to $6,400,000 for 5% daily ATR stop and EOD exit. Arithmetic inconsistent: 25,000*(1+93.50)=2,362,500; 6,400,000/25,000-1=255 (25,500%).

sources.limits: Opening-direction entry is not breakout-stop entry. Headline optimized result is in-sample and expressly assumes zero slippage. Per-trade R normalization and annual return definitions require reconciliation. No daily return file or drawdown timestamps available.

sources.title: Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)
sources.authors: Carlo Zarattini, Andrew Aziz, Andrea Barbon
sources.access: SSRN abstract and all 8 chunks returned for the first 30 PDF pages. Main methods and Tables 1-6 read; later appendix tables not independently inspected.
sources.version: PDF revision 22 September 2025; SSRN lists 43 pages.

facts.rules: Time-varying noise bands from prior 14 sessions; half-hour signal/stop evaluation; current-band plus RTH VWAP exit; final version 2% daily volatility exposure target capped at 4x; commissions $0.0035/share, slippage $0.001/share
facts.reversal_example: 2022-01-20: opposite-band version -2.19%, same-band -0.31%, same-band plus VWAP about 0% (Figures 4-5); not local ORB trades.
facts.gamma_proxy: Section 4.5 uses prior-day five-day RSI, explicitly not a precise gamma estimate; regression coefficient -3.25 bps per RSI point, p=0.001, descriptive not causal proof.

sources.limits: Dynamic-band SPY momentum is not fixed 30-minute ES ORB. Return target/stop sampling differs. Volatility sizing raised MDD from 12% to 25%. Live slippage experiment is a few April 2024 days, not all regimes. Worst trade date is not drawdown episode date.

sources.title: Market Intraday Momentum
sources.authors: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
sources.access: SSRN abstract only for claims here; no complete 48-page PDF audit.
sources.facts: SPY 1993-2013; first half-hour return includes previous-close-to-open component and predicts final half-hour; stronger high-volume, high-volatility and major macro-news days; ten other ETFs. Not evidence for immediate morning breakout execution.

sources.title: Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum
sources.authors: Guido Baltussen, Zhi Da, Sten Lammers, Martin Martens
sources.access: SSRN abstract and publication metadata; not complete 60-page PDF.
sources.facts: More than 60 futures 1974-2020; rest-of-day returns predict final half-hour; links to short-gamma hedging and leveraged ETFs; reversal over subsequent days. Mechanism evidence, not validation of the local ORB.

sources.title: Time Series Momentum
sources.authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
sources.facts: 58 liquid futures; 1-12 month persistence with partial longer-horizon reversal. No direct five-minute ORB inference.

sources.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Marcos Lopez de Prado
sources.access: Author PDF introduction and main method read (chunks 0-3 of 7); Eq. 1-2 verified. Appendices not fully reviewed.
sources.locators: Expected Sharpe Ratios Under Multiple Trials; The Deflated Sharpe Ratio; equations 1-2.
sources.facts: Correct for search selection and non-normality using sample length, return moments, dispersion of trial Sharpe estimates and effective trial count. DSR is not a prop challenge pass probability or SSRN certification.

sources.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Qiji Jim Zhu
sources.access: SSRN search metadata; author PDF abstract, introduction and Section 2.1 read (chunks 0 and 2). Selective method review, not full paper.
sources.facts: Probability that in-sample winner ranks below median out of sample; diagnostic for selection process, not the probability of making money.

sources.title: The Sharpe Ratio Efficient Frontier
sources.authors: David H. Bailey, Marcos Lopez de Prado
sources.access: SSRN abstract; PSR equation cross-checked against source 7.
sources.facts: PSR and minimum track-record length account for sample uncertainty and higher return moments under stated assumptions.

sources.title: The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios
sources.access: SSRN abstract; landing page says not available for download.
sources.facts: Serial correlation changes sampling error and annualization; square-root-of-time rule not generally valid.

sources.title: Day Trading for a Living?
sources.authors: Fernando Chague, Rodrigo De-Losso, Bruno Giovannetti
sources.facts: Brazilian equity-futures beginners 2013-2015: 97% of those persisting more than 300 days lost money. Cohort evidence, not measured failure probability of this ORB.

sources.title: Assessing the profitability of intraday opening range breakout strategies
sources.authors: Ulf Holmberg, Carl Lönnbark, Christian Lundström
sources.access: All 4 retrieved university PDF chunks read. This is supplementary non-SSRN research, not falsely described as an SSRN retrieval.
sources.locators: Sections 2-4 and Table 2 (table extraction degraded; numeric table cells not relied on).
sources.facts: Crude oil 1983-03-30 to 2011-01-26; daily OHLC threshold-crossing model, no stop or target, zero cost/perfect fill assumptions. Ex-post threshold calibration. Final subperiod 2001-10-12 to 2011-01-26 drives results; earlier periods less robust. These are sample partitions, not reported drawdown episodes.

sources.title: Micro E-mini Equity Index futures products overview
sources.facts: ES multiplier $50/point, MES $5/point; quarter-point increments; MES tick $1.25, ES $12.50. Contract limits/margins must be verified at broker.
